tagline: An open observatory of the criminal law of the world and of the crime of genocide
about: Astraea is a surface observatory, with open data, on three things: what the criminal law and the treaties of each country say; what the news publishes about allegations; and what international courts decide.

It does not qualify facts. For each situation it records who asserted what, to what degree, with the source, the date it was read and a level of confidence. A status reads as “provisional measures” followed by the body that ordered them, never as a verdict of ours.
Every piece of data says where it came from. A piece of data without a source is worse than a missing one.
countries_note: A country counts as checked when every field of its record carries a stamp: source, date read, confidence and who checked it. The fields on criminal law and treaties arrive in the next phase.
situations_intro: The highest status recorded for each situation, in the words of the body that issued it. The link goes to the official page that was read.
status_draft: draft: not yet checked by a person
drafts_note: A field in draft was read from its source but has not yet been stamped by a person. The quality report lists each one.
